 Duncan Bannatyne has furiously hit out at actress Nicola Coughlan after she publicly condemned HBO's upcoming adaptation of JK Rowling's Harry Potter books.
 The Bridgerton actress firmly ruled out any involvement with the forthcoming television adaptation, going as far as to refuse to watch it even though she knows some of its stars.
 "I will not be watching the new Harry Potter show, and I would never be in it," she said.
 "Look, I know people that are involved in those shows, and they're nice people and whatever, but it's not for me."
 TRENDING Stories Videos Your Say Duncan Bannatyne has hit out at Nicola Coughlan 
 |
 GETTY The 39-year-old told The Observer that she used to be a fan of the wizarding novels, but Ms Rowling's stance on gender related issues has prompted her to turn her back on the franchise.
 Ms Coughlan's strong words have garnered plenty of attention among the Harry Potter fanbase, and now piqued the interest of business tycoon Mr Bannatyne.
 He slammed the actress on X, writing: "Well, I will not be watching anything with Nicola Coughlan in it from now.
 "I hate people that think it is ok to destroy others even if they could." 
 Nicola Coughlan has publicly condemned JK Rowling over her trans views
 |
 GETTY
 The feud between Ms Rowling and Ms Coughlan isn't exactly new.
 In 2025, when the UK Supreme Court ruled that the legal definition of a woman is based on biological sex, Rowling celebrated on X with a post of her smoking a cigar.
 "I love it when a plan comes together #SupremeCourt #WomensRights," Ms Rowling captioned the post.
 Ms Coughlan subsequently responded by sharing a piece from The Cut headlined "This Is a New Low for JK Rowling" on her Instagram Story, adding: "Keep your new Harry Potter lads. Wouldn't touch it with a 10 foot pole."

 The Last of Us star Pedro Pascal also weighed in, branding Ms Rowling a "heinous loser."
 Ms Rowling then dismissed both actors, claiming on X that she had never heard of either and could not be bothered to look them up.
 Ms Coughlan's boycott comes as several cast members of the series have sought to put distance between themselves and Ms Rowling's stance on gender identity.
 John Lithgow, who takes on the role of Albus Dumbledore, addressed the matter earlier this year, saying: "I find it ironic and somewhat inexplicable that Rowling has expressed such views."
 JK Rowling has faced backlash for her views on gender and biological sex for years |
 PA Paapa Essiedu, cast as Severus Snape, declined to engage with Rowling's politics directly in a recent Vanity Fair profile but was made clear he "believes, in my bones, that trans people, queer people, people of all creeds and color have got the right to be treated with respect and dignity and safety at all times".
 Nick Frost and Bel Powley are among other cast members who have similarly distanced themselves from Ms Rowling's position.
 Ms Rowling serves as an executive producer on the series, which is set to debut its first two episodes on Christmas Day.
 The show is written by Francesca Gardiner and directed by Mark Mylod, both known for their work on Succession.
